verdict.rationale: YYLO is a command-line orchestrator for coding agents. It documents a one-shot, prompt-as-argument invocation (`yy pi --no-session '...'`), JSON watch receipts with `state` and `exit_code`, and intentionally nonzero exit codes, which together support scripted, non-interactive use from shell scripts. Nothing documents running it inside CI/CD pipelines, such as CI configuration examples, non-interactive authentication or an explicit headless mode, so coverage of the story is only partial. Missing for 10: explicit CI/CD pipeline documentation or examples, a documented headless/non-interactive flag and credential handling, and independent hands-on corroboration of CI usage.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run an agent headlessly inside CI/CD pipelines and shell scripts

citations.quote: yy pi --no-session 'Summarize this repository. Do not edit files.'
emits a watch receipt with `"state":"COMPLETED"`, `"exit_code":0`, and nonzero `log_bytes`
YYLO is a command-line orchestrator for coding agents, repeatable workflows, and receipt-backed repository changes.
